audit_status.source_base: Greek Acts text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for Cornelius, Peter vision, clean/common, Spirit direction, Gentile household, no partiality, Spirit falling, baptism.

verses.restored: A certain man in Caesarea named Cornelius, a centurion from the cohort called Italian,

familiar.text: There was a certain man in Caesarea called Cornelius, a centurion of the band called the Italian band,

modern.text: At Caesarea there was a man named Cornelius, a centurion in what was called the Italian Regiment.

original.text: Ἀνὴρ δέ ⸀τις ἐν Καισαρείᾳ ὀνόματι Κορνήλιος, ἑκατοντάρχης ἐκ σπείρης τῆς καλουμένης Ἰταλικῆς,

verses.restored: devout and revering the Divine with all his household, doing many acts of mercy for the people and praying to the Divine continually,

familiar.text: A devout man, and one that feared God with all his house, which gave much alms to the people, and prayed to God alway.

modern.text: He and all his household were devout and God-fearing. He gave generously to the people and prayed to God regularly.

original.text: εὐσεβὴς καὶ φοβούμενος τὸν θεὸν σὺν παντὶ τῷ οἴκῳ αὐτοῦ, ⸀ποιῶν ἐλεημοσύνας πολλὰς τῷ λαῷ καὶ δεόμενος τοῦ θεοῦ διὰ παντός,

verses.restored: saw clearly in a vision, about the ninth hour of the day, a messenger of the Divine coming to him and saying to him, Cornelius.

familiar.text: He saw in a vision evidently about the ninth hour of the day an angel of God coming in to him, and saying unto him, Cornelius.

modern.text: One day at about the ninth hour, he had a clear vision of an angel of God who came to him and said, “Cornelius!”

original.text: εἶδεν ἐν ὁράματι φανερῶς ὡσεὶ ⸀περὶ ὥραν ἐνάτην τῆς ἡμέρας ἄγγελον τοῦ θεοῦ εἰσελθόντα πρὸς αὐτὸν καὶ εἰπόντα αὐτῷ· Κορνήλιε.

verses.restored: Looking intently at him and becoming afraid, he said, What is it, Lord? He said to him, Your prayers and your acts of mercy have gone up as a memorial before the Divine.

familiar.text: And when he looked on him, he was afraid, and said, What is it, Lord? And he said unto him, Thy prayers and thine alms are come up for a memorial before God.

modern.text: Cornelius stared at him in fear and asked, “What is it, Lord?” The angel answered, “Your prayers and gifts to the poor have ascended as a memorial offering before God.

original.text: ὁ δὲ ἀτενίσας αὐτῷ καὶ ἔμφοβος γενόμενος εἶπεν· Τί ἐστιν, κύριε; εἶπεν δὲ αὐτῷ· Αἱ προσευχαί σου καὶ αἱ ἐλεημοσύναι σου ἀνέβησαν εἰς μνημόσυνον ⸀ἔμπροσθεν τοῦ θεοῦ·

verses.restored: Now send men to Joppa and summon a certain Simon who is called Peter.

familiar.text: And now send men to Joppa, and call for one Simon, whose surname is Peter:

modern.text: Now send men to Joppa to call for a man named Simon who is called Peter.

original.text: καὶ νῦν πέμψον ⸂ἄνδρας εἰς Ἰόππην⸃ καὶ μετάπεμψαι Σίμωνά ⸂τινα ὃς ἐπικαλεῖται Πέτρος⸃·

verses.restored: This one is lodging with a certain Simon, a tanner, whose house is by the sea.

familiar.text: He lodgeth with one Simon a tanner, whose house is by the sea side: he shall tell thee what thou oughtest to do.

modern.text: He is staying with Simon the tanner, whose house is by the sea. ”

original.text: οὗτος ξενίζεται παρά τινι Σίμωνι βυρσεῖ, ᾧ ἐστιν οἰκία παρὰ θάλασσαν.

verses.restored: When the messenger speaking to him departed, he called two of his household servants and a devout soldier from those attending him,

familiar.text: And when the angel which spake unto Cornelius was departed, he called two of his household servants, and a devout soldier of them that waited on him continually;

modern.text: When the angel who spoke to him had gone, Cornelius called two of his servants and a devout soldier from among his attendants.

original.text: ὡς δὲ ἀπῆλθεν ὁ ἄγγελος ὁ λαλῶν ⸀αὐτῷ, φωνήσας δύο τῶν ⸀οἰκετῶν καὶ στρατιώτην εὐσεβῆ τῶν προσκαρτερούντων αὐτῷ

verses.restored: and having explained everything to them, he sent them to Joppa.

familiar.text: And when he had declared all these things unto them, he sent them to Joppa.

modern.text: He explained what had happened and sent them to Joppa. Peter’s Vision (Leviticus 11:1–47; Deuteronomy 14:1–21)

original.text: καὶ ἐξηγησάμενος ⸂ἅπαντα αὐτοῖς⸃ ἀπέστειλεν αὐτοὺς εἰς τὴν Ἰόππην.

verses.restored: The next day, as they were journeying and drawing near the city, Peter went up on the housetop to pray about the sixth hour.

familiar.text: On the morrow, as they went on their journey, and drew nigh unto the city, Peter went up upon the housetop to pray about the sixth hour:

modern.text: The next day at about the sixth hour, as the men were approaching the city on their journey, Peter went up on the roof to pray.

original.text: Τῇ δὲ ἐπαύριον ὁδοιπορούντων ἐκείνων καὶ τῇ πόλει ἐγγιζόντων ἀνέβη Πέτρος ἐπὶ τὸ δῶμα προσεύξασθαι περὶ ὥραν ἕκτην.

verses.restored: He became hungry and wanted to taste food. While they were preparing it, a trance came upon him.

familiar.text: And he became very hungry, and would have eaten: but while they made ready, he fell into a trance,

modern.text: He became hungry and wanted something to eat, but while the meal was being prepared, he fell into a trance.

original.text: ἐγένετο δὲ πρόσπεινος καὶ ἤθελεν γεύσασθαι· παρασκευαζόντων δὲ ⸀αὐτῶν ⸀ἐγένετο ἐπʼ αὐτὸν ἔκστασις,

verses.restored: He beholds heaven opened and a certain vessel descending, like a great linen sheet, being lowered by four corners upon the earth.

familiar.text: And saw heaven opened, and a certain vessel descending unto him, as it had been a great sheet knit at the four corners, and let down to the earth:

modern.text: He saw heaven open and something like a large sheet being let down to earth by its four corners.

original.text: καὶ θεωρεῖ τὸν οὐρανὸν ἀνεῳγμένον καὶ ⸀καταβαῖνον σκεῦός τι ὡς ὀθόνην μεγάλην τέσσαρσιν ⸀ἀρχαῖς καθιέμενον ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς,

verses.restored: In it were all the four-footed creatures and reptiles of the earth and birds of heaven.

familiar.text: Wherein were all manner of fourfooted beasts of the earth, and wild beasts, and creeping things, and fowls of the air.

modern.text: It contained all kinds of four-footed animals and reptiles of the earth, as well as birds of the air.

original.text: ἐν ᾧ ὑπῆρχεν πάντα τὰ τετράποδα ⸂καὶ ἑρπετὰ τῆς γῆς καὶ⸃ πετεινὰ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ.

verses.restored: A voice came to him, Rise, Peter; slaughter and eat.

familiar.text: And there came a voice to him, Rise, Peter; kill, and eat.

modern.text: Then a voice said to him: “Get up, Peter, kill and eat!”

original.text: καὶ ἐγένετο φωνὴ πρὸς αὐτόν· Ἀναστάς, Πέτρε, θῦσον καὶ φάγε.

verses.restored: But Peter said, By no means, Lord, because I have never eaten anything common or unclean.

familiar.text: But Peter said, Not so, Lord; for I have never eaten any thing that is common or unclean.

modern.text: “No, Lord!” Peter answered. “I have never eaten anything impure or unclean.”

original.text: ὁ δὲ Πέτρος εἶπεν· Μηδαμῶς, κύριε, ὅτι οὐδέποτε ἔφαγον πᾶν κοινὸν ⸀καὶ ἀκάθαρτον.

verses.restored: A voice came again a second time to him, What the Divine cleansed, you must not make common.

familiar.text: And the voice spake unto him again the second time, What God hath cleansed, that call not thou common.

modern.text: The voice spoke to him a second time: “Do not call anything impure that God has made clean.”

original.text: καὶ φωνὴ πάλιν ἐκ δευτέρου πρὸς αὐτόν· Ἃ ὁ θεὸς ἐκαθάρισεν σὺ μὴ κοίνου.

verses.restored: This happened three times, and immediately the vessel was taken up into heaven.

familiar.text: This was done thrice: and the vessel was received up again into heaven.

modern.text: This happened three times, and all at once the sheet was taken back up into heaven. Peter Called to Caesarea

original.text: τοῦτο δὲ ἐγένετο ἐπὶ τρίς, καὶ ⸀εὐθὺς ἀνελήμφθη τὸ σκεῦος εἰς τὸν οὐρανόν.

verses.restored: As Peter was thoroughly perplexed in himself about what the vision he saw might mean, look, the men sent by Cornelius, having asked for Simon's house, stood at the gate.

familiar.text: Now while Peter doubted in himself what this vision which he had seen should mean, behold, the men which were sent from Cornelius had made enquiry for Simon’s house, and stood before the gate,

modern.text: While Peter was puzzling over the meaning of the vision, the men sent by Cornelius found Simon’s house and approached the gate.

original.text: Ὡς δὲ ἐν ἑαυτῷ διηπόρει ὁ Πέτρος τί ἂν εἴη τὸ ὅραμα ὃ εἶδεν, ⸀ἰδοὺ οἱ ἄνδρες οἱ ἀπεσταλμένοι ⸀ὑπὸ τοῦ Κορνηλίου διερωτήσαντες τὴν οἰκίαν ⸀τοῦ Σίμωνος ἐπέστησαν ἐπὶ τὸν πυλῶνα,

verses.restored: Calling out, they were asking whether Simon called Peter was lodging there.

familiar.text: And called, and asked whether Simon, which was surnamed Peter, were lodged there.

modern.text: They called out to ask if Simon called Peter was staying there.

original.text: καὶ φωνήσαντες ⸀ἐπυνθάνοντο εἰ Σίμων ὁ ἐπικαλούμενος Πέτρος ἐνθάδε ξενίζεται.

verses.restored: While Peter was pondering the vision, the Spirit said to him, Look, three men are seeking you.

familiar.text: While Peter thought on the vision, the Spirit said unto him, Behold, three men seek thee.

modern.text: As Peter continued to reflect on the vision, the Spirit said to him, “Behold, three men are looking for you.

original.text: τοῦ δὲ Πέτρου διενθυμουμένου περὶ τοῦ ὁράματος εἶπεν ⸂αὐτῷ τὸ πνεῦμα⸃· Ἰδοὺ ⸀ἄνδρες ⸀ζητοῦντές σε·

verses.restored: But rise, go down, and go with them, making no distinction, because I have sent them.

familiar.text: Arise therefore, and get thee down, and go with them, doubting nothing: for I have sent them.

modern.text: So get up! Go downstairs and accompany them without hesitation, because I have sent them.”

original.text: ἀλλὰ ἀναστὰς κατάβηθι καὶ πορεύου σὺν αὐτοῖς μηδὲν διακρινόμενος, ⸀ὅτι ἐγὼ ἀπέσταλκα αὐτούς.

verses.restored: Peter went down to the men and said, Look, I am the one you seek. What is the cause for which you are here?

familiar.text: Then Peter went down to the men which were sent unto him from Cornelius; and said, Behold, I am he whom ye seek: what is the cause wherefore ye are come?

modern.text: So Peter went down to the men and said, “Here am I, the one you are looking for. Why have you come?”

original.text: καταβὰς δὲ Πέτρος πρὸς τοὺς ἄνδρας εἶπεν· Ἰδοὺ ἐγώ εἰμι ὃν ζητεῖτε· τίς ἡ αἰτία διʼ ἣν πάρεστε;

verses.restored: They said, Cornelius, a centurion, a righteous man and one revering the Divine, witnessed by the whole nation of the Judeans, was instructed by a holy messenger to summon you to his house and hear words from you.

familiar.text: And they said, Cornelius the centurion, a just man, and one that feareth God, and of good report among all the nation of the Jews, was warned from God by an holy angel to send for thee into his house, and to hear words of thee.

modern.text: “Cornelius the centurion has sent us,” they said. “He is a righteous and God-fearing man with a good reputation among the whole Jewish nation. A holy angel instructed him to request your presence in his home so he could hear a message from you.”

original.text: οἱ δὲ εἶπαν· Κορνήλιος ἑκατοντάρχης, ἀνὴρ δίκαιος καὶ φοβούμενος τὸν θεὸν μαρτυρούμενός τε ὑπὸ ὅλου τοῦ ἔθνους τῶν Ἰουδαίων, ἐχρηματίσθη ὑπὸ ἀγγέλου ἁγίου μεταπέμψασθαί σε εἰς τὸν οἶκον αὐτοῦ καὶ ἀκοῦσαι ῥήματα παρὰ σοῦ.

verses.restored: Therefore inviting them in, he lodged them. The next day, rising, he went with them, and some of the siblings from Joppa went with him.

familiar.text: Then called he them in, and lodged them. And on the morrow Peter went away with them, and certain brethren from Joppa accompanied him.

modern.text: So Peter invited them in as his guests. And the next day he got ready and went with them, accompanied by some of the brothers from Joppa. Peter Visits Cornelius

original.text: εἰσκαλεσάμενος οὖν αὐτοὺς ἐξένισεν. Τῇ δὲ ἐπαύριον ⸀ἀναστὰς ἐξῆλθεν σὺν αὐτοῖς, καί τινες τῶν ἀδελφῶν τῶν ἀπὸ Ἰόππης συνῆλθον αὐτῷ.

verses.restored: The next day he entered Caesarea. Cornelius was expecting them, having called together his relatives and close friends.

familiar.text: And the morrow after they entered into Caesarea. And Cornelius waited for them, and had called together his kinsmen and near friends.

modern.text: The following day he arrived in Caesarea, where Cornelius was expecting them and had called together his relatives and close friends.

original.text: ⸂τῇ δὲ⸃ ἐπαύριον ⸀εἰσῆλθεν εἰς τὴν Καισάρειαν. ὁ δὲ Κορνήλιος ἦν προσδοκῶν αὐτοὺς συγκαλεσάμενος τοὺς συγγενεῖς αὐτοῦ καὶ τοὺς ἀναγκαίους φίλους.

verses.restored: When Peter entered, Cornelius met him, fell at his feet, and worshiped.

familiar.text: And as Peter was coming in, Cornelius met him, and fell down at his feet, and worshipped him.

modern.text: As Peter was about to enter, Cornelius met him and fell at his feet to worship him.

original.text: ὡς δὲ ἐγένετο τοῦ εἰσελθεῖν τὸν Πέτρον, συναντήσας αὐτῷ ὁ Κορνήλιος πεσὼν ἐπὶ τοὺς πόδας προσεκύνησεν.

verses.restored: But Peter raised him, saying, Stand up; I myself also am human.

familiar.text: But Peter took him up, saying, Stand up; I myself also am a man.

modern.text: But Peter helped him up. “Stand up,” he said, “I am only a man myself.”

original.text: ὁ δὲ Πέτρος ⸂ἤγειρεν αὐτὸν⸃ λέγων· Ἀνάστηθι· καὶ ἐγὼ αὐτὸς ἄνθρωπός εἰμι.

verses.restored: Conversing with him, he entered and finds many gathered together.

familiar.text: And as he talked with him, he went in, and found many that were come together.

modern.text: As Peter talked with him, he went inside and found many people gathered together.

original.text: καὶ συνομιλῶν αὐτῷ εἰσῆλθεν, καὶ εὑρίσκει συνεληλυθότας πολλούς,

verses.restored: He said to them, You yourselves know how unlawful it is for a Judean man to join or come to one of another people; and yet the Divine showed me to call no human common or unclean.

familiar.text: And he said unto them, Ye know how that it is an unlawful thing for a man that is a Jew to keep company, or come unto one of another nation; but God hath shewed me that I should not call any man common or unclean.

modern.text: He said to them, “You know how unlawful it is for a Jew to associate with a foreigner or visit him. But God has shown me that I should not call any man impure or unclean.

original.text: ἔφη τε πρὸς αὐτούς· Ὑμεῖς ἐπίστασθε ὡς ἀθέμιτόν ἐστιν ἀνδρὶ Ἰουδαίῳ κολλᾶσθαι ἢ προσέρχεσθαι ἀλλοφύλῳ· κἀμοὶ ὁ θεὸς ἔδειξεν μηδένα κοινὸν ἢ ἀκάθαρτον λέγειν ἄνθρωπον·

verses.restored: Therefore I came without objection when summoned. I ask then, for what reason did you summon me?

familiar.text: Therefore came I unto you without gainsaying, as soon as I was sent for: I ask therefore for what intent ye have sent for me?

modern.text: So when I was invited, I came without objection. I ask, then, why have you sent for me?”

original.text: διὸ καὶ ἀναντιρρήτως ἦλθον μεταπεμφθείς. πυνθάνομαι οὖν τίνι λόγῳ μετεπέμψασθέ με.

verses.restored: Cornelius said, Four days ago until this hour I was praying the ninth hour in my house, and look, a man stood before me in bright clothing,

familiar.text: And Cornelius said, Four days ago I was fasting until this hour; and at the ninth hour I prayed in my house, and, behold, a man stood before me in bright clothing,

modern.text: Cornelius answered: “Four days ago I was in my house praying at this, the ninth hour. Suddenly a man in radiant clothing stood before me

original.text: Καὶ ὁ Κορνήλιος ἔφη· Ἀπὸ τετάρτης ἡμέρας μέχρι ταύτης τῆς ὥρας ⸀ἤμην τὴν ⸀ἐνάτην προσευχόμενος ἐν τῷ οἴκῳ μου, καὶ ἰδοὺ ἀνὴρ ἔστη ἐνώπιόν μου ἐν ἐσθῆτι λαμπρᾷ

verses.restored: and said, Cornelius, your prayer was heard, and your acts of mercy were remembered before the Divine.

familiar.text: And said, Cornelius, thy prayer is heard, and thine alms are had in remembrance in the sight of God.

modern.text: and said, ‘Cornelius, your prayer has been heard, and your gifts to the poor have been remembered before God.

original.text: καὶ φησί· Κορνήλιε, εἰσηκούσθη σου ἡ προσευχὴ καὶ αἱ ἐλεημοσύναι σου ἐμνήσθησαν ἐνώπιον τοῦ θεοῦ.

verses.restored: Send therefore to Joppa and summon Simon who is called Peter; this one is lodging in the house of Simon, a tanner, by the sea.

familiar.text: Send therefore to Joppa, and call hither Simon, whose surname is Peter; he is lodged in the house of one Simon a tanner by the sea side: who, when he cometh, shall speak unto thee.

modern.text: Therefore send to Joppa for Simon, who is called Peter. He is a guest in the home of Simon the tanner, by the sea.’

original.text: πέμψον οὖν εἰς Ἰόππην καὶ μετακάλεσαι Σίμωνα ὃς ἐπικαλεῖται Πέτρος· οὗτος ξενίζεται ἐν οἰκίᾳ Σίμωνος βυρσέως παρὰ ⸀θάλασσαν.

verses.restored: Therefore immediately I sent to you, and you did beautifully/well in coming. Now therefore we are all present before the Divine to hear all the things commanded to you by the Lord.

familiar.text: Immediately therefore I sent to thee; and thou hast well done that thou art come. Now therefore are we all here present before God, to hear all things that are commanded thee of God.

modern.text: So I sent for you immediately, and you were kind enough to come. Now then, we are all here in the presence of God to listen to everything the Lord has instructed you to tell us.” Good News for the Gentiles

original.text: ἐξαυτῆς οὖν ἔπεμψα πρὸς σέ, σύ τε καλῶς ἐποίησας παραγενόμενος. νῦν οὖν πάντες ἡμεῖς ἐνώπιον τοῦ θεοῦ πάρεσμεν ἀκοῦσαι πάντα τὰ προστεταγμένα σοι ὑπὸ τοῦ ⸀κυρίου.

verses.restored: Opening his mouth, Peter said, In truth I grasp that the Divine is not one who shows partiality,

familiar.text: Then Peter opened his mouth, and said, Of a truth I perceive that God is no respecter of persons:

modern.text: Then Peter began to speak: “I now truly understand that God does not show favoritism,

original.text: Ἀνοίξας δὲ Πέτρος τὸ στόμα εἶπεν· Ἐπʼ ἀληθείας καταλαμβάνομαι ὅτι οὐκ ἔστιν προσωπολήμπτης ὁ θεός,

verses.restored: but in every nation the one revering him and working righteousness/justice is acceptable to him.

familiar.text: But in every nation he that feareth him, and worketh righteousness, is accepted with him.

modern.text: but welcomes those from every nation who fear Him and do what is right.

original.text: ἀλλʼ ἐν παντὶ ἔθνει ὁ φοβούμενος αὐτὸν καὶ ἐργαζόμενος δικαιοσύνην δεκτὸς αὐτῷ ἐστιν.

verses.restored: The word he sent to the children of Israel, announcing good news of peace through Jesus Messiah—this one is Lord of all—

familiar.text: The word which God sent unto the children of Israel, preaching peace by Jesus Christ: (he is Lord of all:)

modern.text: He has sent this message to the people of Israel, proclaiming the gospel of peace through Jesus Christ, who is Lord of all.

original.text: τὸν λόγον ⸀ὃν ἀπέστειλεν τοῖς υἱοῖς Ἰσραὴλ εὐαγγελιζόμενος εἰρήνην διὰ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ· οὗτός ἐστιν πάντων κύριος.

verses.restored: you know the word that happened throughout all Judea, beginning from Galilee after the baptism John proclaimed:

familiar.text: That word, I say, ye know, which was published throughout all Judaea, and began from Galilee, after the baptism which John preached;

modern.text: You yourselves know what has happened throughout Judea, beginning in Galilee with the baptism that John proclaimed:

original.text: ὑμεῖς οἴδατε τὸ γενόμενον ῥῆμα καθʼ ὅλης τῆς Ἰουδαίας, ⸀ἀρξάμενος ἀπὸ τῆς Γαλιλαίας μετὰ τὸ βάπτισμα ὃ ἐκήρυξεν Ἰωάννης,

verses.restored: Jesus from Nazareth, how the Divine anointed him with holy Spirit and power, who went about doing good and healing all those oppressed by the adversarial force, because the Divine was with him.

familiar.text: How God anointed Jesus of Nazareth with the Holy Ghost and with power: who went about doing good, and healing all that were oppressed of the devil; for God was with him.

modern.text: how God anointed Jesus of Nazareth with the Holy Spirit and with power, and how Jesus went around doing good and healing all who were oppressed by the devil, because God was with Him.

original.text: Ἰησοῦν τὸν ἀπὸ Ναζαρέθ, ὡς ἔχρισεν αὐτὸν ὁ θεὸς πνεύματι ἁγίῳ καὶ δυνάμει, ὃς διῆλθεν εὐεργετῶν καὶ ἰώμενος πάντας τοὺς καταδυναστευομένους ὑπὸ τοῦ διαβόλου, ὅτι ὁ θεὸς ἦν μετʼ αὐτοῦ·

verses.restored: We are witnesses of all things he did both in the country of the Judeans and in Jerusalem; whom they also killed, hanging him on a tree.

familiar.text: And we are witnesses of all things which he did both in the land of the Jews, and in Jerusalem; whom they slew and hanged on a tree:

modern.text: We are witnesses of all that He did, both in the land of the Jews and in Jerusalem. And although they put Him to death by hanging Him on a tree,

original.text: καὶ ⸀ἡμεῖς μάρτυρες πάντων ὧν ἐποίησεν ἔν τε τῇ χώρᾳ τῶν Ἰουδαίων ⸀καὶ Ἰερουσαλήμ· ὃν καὶ ἀνεῖλαν κρεμάσαντες ἐπὶ ξύλου.

verses.restored: This one the Divine raised on the third day and gave him to become manifest,

familiar.text: Him God raised up the third day, and shewed him openly;

modern.text: God raised Him up on the third day and caused Him to be seen—

original.text: τοῦτον ὁ θεὸς ἤγειρεν ⸀τῇ τρίτῃ ἡμέρᾳ καὶ ἔδωκεν αὐτὸν ἐμφανῆ γενέσθαι,

verses.restored: not to all the people, but to witnesses appointed beforehand by the Divine, to us who ate and drank with him after he rose from the dead.

familiar.text: Not to all the people, but unto witnesses chosen before of God, even to us, who did eat and drink with him after he rose from the dead.

modern.text: not by all the people, but by the witnesses God had chosen beforehand, by us who ate and drank with Him after He rose from the dead.

original.text: οὐ παντὶ τῷ λαῷ ἀλλὰ μάρτυσι τοῖς προκεχειροτονημένοις ὑπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ, ἡμῖν, οἵτινες συνεφάγομεν καὶ συνεπίομεν αὐτῷ μετὰ τὸ ἀναστῆναι αὐτὸν ἐκ νεκρῶν·

verses.restored: He commanded us to proclaim to the people and to testify that this is the one appointed by the Divine as judge of living and dead.

familiar.text: And he commanded us to preach unto the people, and to testify that it is he which was ordained of God to be the Judge of quick and dead.

modern.text: And He commanded us to preach to the people and to testify that He is the One appointed by God to judge the living and the dead.

original.text: καὶ παρήγγειλεν ἡμῖν κηρύξαι τῷ λαῷ καὶ διαμαρτύρασθαι ὅτι ⸀οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ ὡρισμένος ὑπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ κριτὴς ζώντων καὶ νεκρῶν.

verses.restored: To this one all the prophets bear witness, that everyone trusting into him receives release of sins/misalignments through his name.

familiar.text: To him give all the prophets witness, that through his name whosoever believeth in him shall receive remission of sins.

modern.text: All the prophets testify about Him that everyone who believes in Him receives forgiveness of sins through His name.” The Gentiles Receive the Holy Spirit (Acts 19:1–7)

original.text: τούτῳ πάντες οἱ προφῆται μαρτυροῦσιν, ἄφεσιν ἁμαρτιῶν λαβεῖν διὰ τοῦ ὀνόματος αὐτοῦ πάντα τὸν πιστεύοντα εἰς αὐτόν.

verses.restored: While Peter was still speaking these words, the holy Spirit fell upon all those hearing the word.

familiar.text: While Peter yet spake these words, the Holy Ghost fell on all them which heard the word.

modern.text: While Peter was still speaking these words, the Holy Spirit fell upon all who heard his message.

original.text: Ἔτι λαλοῦντος τοῦ Πέτρου τὰ ῥήματα ταῦτα ἐπέπεσε τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον ἐπὶ πάντας τοὺς ἀκούοντας τὸν λόγον.

verses.restored: The trusting ones from circumcision, as many as came with Peter, were amazed because the gift of the holy Spirit had been poured out also upon the nations.

familiar.text: And they of the circumcision which believed were astonished, as many as came with Peter, because that on the Gentiles also was poured out the gift of the Holy Ghost.

modern.text: All the circumcised believers who had accompanied Peter were astounded that the gift of the Holy Spirit had been poured out even on the Gentiles.

original.text: καὶ ἐξέστησαν οἱ ἐκ περιτομῆς πιστοὶ ⸀ὅσοι συνῆλθαν τῷ Πέτρῳ, ὅτι καὶ ἐπὶ τὰ ἔθνη ἡ δωρεὰ τοῦ ⸂ἁγίου πνεύματος⸃ ἐκκέχυται·

verses.restored: For they were hearing them speaking in tongues and magnifying the Divine. Then Peter answered,

familiar.text: For they heard them speak with tongues, and magnify God. Then answered Peter,

modern.text: For they heard them speaking in tongues and exalting God. Then Peter said,

original.text: ἤκουον γὰρ αὐτῶν λαλούντων γλώσσαις καὶ μεγαλυνόντων τὸν θεόν. τότε ⸀ἀπεκρίθη Πέτρος·

verses.restored: Can anyone withhold the water, that these should not be baptized, who received the holy Spirit just as we also did?

familiar.text: Can any man forbid water, that these should not be baptized, which have received the Holy Ghost as well as we?

modern.text: “Can anyone withhold the water to baptize these people? They have received the Holy Spirit just as we have!”

original.text: Μήτι τὸ ὕδωρ ⸂δύναται κωλῦσαί⸃ τις τοῦ μὴ βαπτισθῆναι τούτους οἵτινες τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον ἔλαβον ⸀ὡς καὶ ἡμεῖς;

verses.restored: He commanded them to be baptized in the name of Jesus Messiah. Then they asked him to remain some days.

familiar.text: And he commanded them to be baptized in the name of the Lord. Then prayed they him to tarry certain days.

modern.text: So he ordered that they be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ. Then they asked him to stay for a few days.

original.text: προσέταξεν ⸀δὲ αὐτοὺς ⸂ἐν τῷ ὀνόματι Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ βαπτισθῆναι⸃. τότε ἠρώτησαν αὐτὸν ἐπιμεῖναι ἡμέρας τινάς.
